concepts.why: The patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis and presents with scaly erythematous plaques on the lateral leg.
The patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis and presents with symptoms consistent with the disease.
The patient presents with violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, periungual skin, and chest, consistent with psoriatic arthritis.
The patient presents with photodistributed poikiloderma on the chest, consistent with dermatomyositis-associated skin disease.
The patient presents with fatigue and difficulty picking up her child and climbing stairs, consistent with muscle weakness.
The patient presents with diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids, consistent with inflammatory skin disease.
The patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis and presents with normal creatine kinase levels, consistent with autoimmune myopathy.
The patient presents with photodistributed poikiloderma on the chest, consistent with skin manifestations of autoimmune disease.
